sentences.text: If you dig a channel and lay a plank across, you have a bridge.
But a cart loaded with stone rolls on and the plank snaps.
So you build stone piers in the river and rest flat slabs on top.
But stone is typically about 10 to 20 times stronger in compression than in tension, so a long slab cracks underneath.
So you set a wooden frame, curve wedge stones over it, and lock the top with a keystone.
The weight squeezes the stones down the curve into the piers, so the Pons Fabricius still carries walkers after more than 2000 years.
So you pull the frame away, and the arch holds itself, as at Alcántara, where granite blocks sit without mortar.
And the Roman arch is not what everyone thinks, because the Romans did not invent it.
Mesopotamian builders were using brick arches about 4000 years ago, in drains and small structures.
Add a stone road and low walls over the arches, and a cart rolls across.
Congratulations, you have built an arch bridge.
